extracted.intended_audience: attorneys/agents seeking reinstatement to practice before the USPTO; Office of Enrollment and Discipline practitioners
extracted.subtask_description: Decision on a petition for reinstatement to practice before the United States Patent and Trademark Office under 37 C.F.R. § 11.58, describing the materials considered and the outcome (grant).

rubrics_metrics.name: Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58
rubrics_metrics.description: A Petition for Reinstatement must be supported by an Affidavit submitted pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision explicitly notes that Mr. Oldham "has filed an Affidavit pursuant to 37 C.F.R. § 11.58 in support of the Petition." Inclusion of such an affidavit is presented as a required supporting document for a reinstatement petition.

rubrics_metrics.name: Comprehensive review of petition and record material relevant to eligibility
rubrics_metrics.description: The determination on reinstatement is based on a careful review of the Petition, the supporting affidavit, and all information in the record material to the applicant's eligibility for reinstatement.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The Office evaluates the petition by reviewing the submitted petition, supporting affidavit(s), and every item in the record that bears on eligibility. The phrasing emphasizes a thorough, record-focused inquiry: "careful review of the Petition, the supporting affidavit, and all information in the record material to his eligibility for reinstatement."

rubrics_metrics.name: Director's discretionary determination of appropriateness
rubrics_metrics.description: The Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline (or delegated official) has the authority to determine whether reinstatement is appropriate and to grant or deny the Petition.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: The decision states that, after review, "the Director of the Office of Enrollment and Discipline has determined that reinstatement ... is appropriate. Accordingly, the Petition is hereby GRANTED." This indicates the Director's discretionary role in weighing the materials and issuing the final decision, reflected by the formal signed order and date.
